title: Glinda The Good Witch Grants Dorothy’s Wish, part 4
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: Glinda the Good stepped down from her ruby throne to give the little girl a good-bye kiss, and Dorothy thanked her for all the kindness she had shown to her friends and herself.
Dorothy now took Toto up solemnly in her arms, and having said one last good-bye she clapped the heels of her shoes together three times, saying:
Instantly she was whirling through the air, so swiftly that all she could see or feel was the wind whistling past her ears.
The Silver Shoes took but three steps, and then she stopped so suddenly that she rolled over upon the grass several times before she knew where she was.
At length, however, she sat up and looked about her.

For she was sitting on the broad Kansas prairie, and just before her was the new farmhouse Uncle Henry built after the cyclone had carried away the old one. Uncle Henry was milking the cows in the barnyard, and Toto had jumped out of her arms and was running toward the barn, barking furiously.
Dorothy stood up and found she was in her stocking-feet. For the Silver Shoes had fallen off in her flight through the air, and were lost forever in the desert.
Aunt Em had just come out of the house to water the cabbages when she looked up and saw Dorothy running toward her.
“My darling child!” she cried, folding the little girl in her arms and covering her face with kisses. “Where in the world did you come from?”
“From the Land of Oz,” said Dorothy gravely. “And here is Toto, too. And oh, Aunt Em! I’m so glad to be at home again!”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy say to the Shoes?
options: Take me home to Aunt Em!
Carry me over the desert!
Three steps to Kansas!
Home, and be quick!

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what could Dorothy see or feel as she flew?
options: Only the wind whistling past her ears
The desert passing far below
Glinda's Castle growing smaller
Nothing at all; she had shut her eyes

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did she land?
options: On the broad Kansas prairie
In the middle of the great desert
Beside the old farmhouse ruins
At the edge of the Munchkin country

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what had Uncle Henry built after the cyclone?
options: A new farmhouse
A deeper cyclone cellar
A barn for the cows
A fence of blue

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Silver Shoes?
options: They fell off and were lost in the desert
They turned to plain leather
Glinda kept them at the Castle
Dorothy gave them to the Monkeys

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what was Uncle Henry doing when she arrived?
options: Milking the cows in the barnyard
Watering the cabbages by the house
Mending the roof of the new farmhouse
Searching the prairie for Dorothy

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what was Aunt Em doing?
options: Coming out of the house to water the cabbages
Sitting in the doorway watching the sky
Washing the dishes as she had before
Hiding in the cyclone cellar again

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Toto behave on arrival?
options: Jumped from her arms and ran barking to the barn
Stayed close beside her, too frightened to move
Ran straight to Aunt Em to be petted
Was nowhere to be found at all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does solemnly describe about taking up Toto?
options: Seriously, as befits the moment
Quickly, before he could escape
Sadly, as though sorry to go
Roughly, because she was in haste

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Three steps end the journey, and the ordinary world is waiting
The Silver Shoes fail and leave Dorothy in the desert
Dorothy arrives to find the old farmhouse still standing
Aunt Em refuses to believe where Dorothy has been

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Glinda do before Dorothy left?
options: Stepped down from her throne to kiss her
Gave her back the Golden Cap
Called the Winged Monkeys at once
Walked with her to the Castle gate

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how did Dorothy stop at the end of the flight?
options: So suddenly that she rolled over on the grass
Gently, setting down on her feet
In the air, and had to climb down
Not at all, until Aunt Em caught her

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy find about her feet?
options: She was in her stocking-feet
The Shoes had turned to silver dust
Her old leather shoes were back
Her feet were bare and sore

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Aunt Em ask her?
options: Where in the world she had come from
Whether she had been hurt in the storm
Why she had stayed away so long
What had become of her silver shoes

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Dorothy answer that question?
options: Gravely, saying she came from the Land of Oz
By bursting into tears without a word
By telling the whole story at once
By pretending she could not remember

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does at length mean?
options: After a while
In great detail
Lying full length
For a long time

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A journey of three steps ends in a kiss on the Kansas prairie
A journey that leaves Dorothy stranded far from home
A homecoming in which nobody recognises Dorothy
A last farewell that Dorothy cannot bring herself to make
